title: Do ten divided by nine and one hundred divided by eleven end?
description: Two more divisions are done place by place, and in each one the leftover comes back, so neither ends. Keeko doubts that one hundred divided by eleven is nine point nine.
teaching_notes: One idea: a leftover that comes back brings the same digits back. Watch for children who write a digit in a place where the quotient digit is zero.

video_script.why: The child has seen ten divided by three never end and now meets two more divisions where the leftover comes back, one of them with a zero in the quotient.
video_script.substitution: the book's own two divisions, ten by nine and one hundred by eleven, solved place by place
video_script.anchor: Two divisions: ten divided by nine, and one hundred divided by eleven
video_script.wrong_answer: one hundred divided by eleven is nine point nine
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip writes nine in the tenths place as well and gets nine point nine. Eleven times nine point nine is one hundred and eight point nine, which is more than one hundred.
video_script.payoff_line: Neither division comes to an end.

final_answer.spoken: one point one one one, and nine point zero nine zero nine, and neither ends

maths_rules: 10 ÷ 9: 9 × 1 = 9 and 10 − 9 = 1, so 1 One and 1 One remains
1 One = 10 Tenths; 10 Tenths ÷ 9 gives 1 Tenth with 1 Tenth left, again and again, so 10 ÷ 9 = 1.111...
100 ÷ 11: 11 × 9 = 99 and 100 − 99 = 1, so 9 Ones and 1 One remains
1 One = 10 Tenths; 11 does not go into 10, so 0 Tenths and 10 Tenths remain, which is 100 Hundredths
100 Hundredths ÷ 11: 11 × 9 = 99, so 9 Hundredths and 1 Hundredth remains; the steps repeat, so 100 ÷ 11 = 9.0909...
the slip: 11 × 9.9 = 108.9, which is more than 100
video_script.design: One idea: a leftover that comes back brings the same digits back, so neither division ends. Assumes the long division of ten by three. Wrong idea: writing nine in the tenths place instead of zero. The two divisions stay all video; the working builds place by place; the quotients appear only on the answer beat.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>The leftover is one again, so the same step repeats, and the ones go on for ever.
